scenario: AITA for giving my girlfriend pointers on how to cook better? | So my girlfriend is pissed at me and has a cooking "strike" because, and I quote,"if you are so much better than me at cooking you can do it yourself". We moved in together 6 months ago (been together for 2 before it) and we came to an agreement that she will do the cooking since she comes 2h earlier from work and I was all on board for having a hot meal ready when I come home. The thing is she is not exactly good at it. She isnt terrible, everything she makes is edible but is far off from the standard I was used to. So, I started to give her pointers. After all she cant get better if she doesnt know that something is off. I would tell her whenever she used too little salt or too much spice, if something was a little burnt or undercooked, told her when I knew how to make the dish better next time etc. I would always eat all of it and say thank you so it was not like I was being rude about it. The thing is that she "snapped" when my mother came to visit and I casually said that she could give my girlfriend some cooking advice. My girlfriend nodded and smiled and generally seemed fine in the moment but as soon as the doors closed behind my mother my girlfriend went ballistic, accused me of humiliating her and her cooking in front of my family and stormed off. Since then I apologised saying that I am sorry for giving her constructive criticism in front of my mom but it didnt calm her much and she still refuses to make anything food-related at home for me. I think she is overreacting, I never complained about her cooking or throw it out. I was just being helpful. I miss her cooking, not gonna lie, so I might as well ask here if I stepped over the line somewhere. AITA or is my girlfriend crazy?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I should consider myself an AITA (Asshole in This Argument) or if my girlfriend is overreacting. Let me start by understanding the situation. We've been together for 2 years, and we moved in together 6 months ago. We agreed that she would handle cooking because she gets home earlier from work, and I was happy with that arrangement because it meant I'd have a hot meal ready when I got home. However, she's not the best cook. Her food is edible, but it's far from what I was used to. I started giving her pointers, thinking it would help her improve. I always ate everything and said thank you, so I didn't think I was being rude. Then, when my mom came over, I casually mentioned that she could give my girlfriend some cooking advice. My girlfriend seemed fine at the time, but as soon as my mom left, she went ballistic, accusing me of humiliating her and her cooking in front of my family. She's been refusing to cook anything for me since then. I think she's overreacting because I never complained about her cooking or threw it out. I was just trying to be helpful. But maybe I crossed a line somewhere. Am I the asshole, or is my girlfriend overreacting? First, I need to consider the dynamics of our relationship. We've been together for a while, and moving in together is a significant step. Cooking is a part of our routine, and she took on that responsibility. It's possible that she feels pressure or stress about meeting my expectations, especially since she's not as confident in her cooking skills. When I started giving her pointers, I thought it was constructive. But maybe she felt criticized or belittled. Even though I always ate everything and said thank you, the act of pointing out what could be better might have made her feel inadequate, especially in front of my mom. I should also think about how she perceives my criticism. Maybe she's sensitive about her cooking, and any suggestion that it's not up to standard feels like a personal attack. It's possible that she felt humiliated when I suggested my mom could help, even if I didn't mean it that way. On the other hand, I was trying to be helpful and improve the situation. I didn't mean to hurt her feelings, and I was just sharing my thoughts on how things could be better. It's a fine line between constructive criticism and being perceived as critical. I also need to consider how she's reacting now. She's refusing to cook anything for me, which is a significant change. It might be a way for her to express her frustration and hurt feelings. She might feel that I don't appreciate her efforts or that I'm not supportive of her in front of my family. Maybe I should reflect on how I delivered the criticism. Was it in a way that was supportive and encouraging, or did it come off as judgmental? It's possible that the way I phrased things or the timing of my suggestions made her feel attacked. I also need to think about the bigger picture. Our relationship is important, and communication is key. If she feels that I'm not respecting her or her efforts, that could lead to bigger issues down the line. It might be worth having an open and honest conversation about how we both feel and how we can work together to improve our situation. In the end, I don't think either of us is entirely right or wrong. It's a matter of perspective and how we communicate our needs and feelings. I need to be more mindful of how I approach giving feedback and ensure that she feels supported and appreciated, not criticized or belittled.
